input.brief: Assessor financeiro de IA 24h no WhatsApp com Open Finance, B3 ao vivo, leitura de comprovantes Vision e Google Agenda

direction.name: The product performs
direction.idea: Software is most convincing when it is doing its job in front of you. Instead of describing features, put small, true, working fragments of the product on the page: the actual control, with real content, responding to the pointer. A colour picker's loupe reads the page's own background and prints its value. A list tool lets you tick an item right there. A type-scale plugin sets the page's own headings. Find the one interaction that is the product and make the hero that interaction; then show each further capability as another fragment at real size. No dashboard collage, no browser frame, no screenshots shrunk until unreadable.
direction.composition: Hero: a short plain headline (4–6vw, left-aligned, upper-left third) and one sentence; the rest of the first screen is the main fragment at actual interface size, sitting directly on the page or on one flat stage colour, large enough to read every label. The fragment is built in HTML and works. Below, capabilities are a single-column sequence, each a row of two parts on a 5/7 split: a two-line statement on one side and the relevant fragment on the other, with the fragments varying in size and shape so the column never becomes a zigzag of equal blocks. Fragments are cropped pieces of interface (a menu, a row, a control, a panel edge), not whole windows. One section pins a fragment while three short statements change it.
direction.typography: The marketing type matches the product's interface type so the fragments and the page feel like one thing. Headline modest; interface text at its true size (13–15px) inside fragments.
direction.colour: Neutral ground. The product's own interface colours provide the colour. At most one flat stage colour behind fragments.
direction.imagery: The interface fragments are the main imagery: build them carefully with real labels, real numbers and sensible states (one hovered, one selected). Around them, two or three real pictures of the customer's world (found with scripts/assets.mjs), never stock of people at laptops.
direction.richness: Fidelity. A fragment with believable content and a real hover state is more interesting than any illustration. Spend the effort there.
direction.pitfalls: A fake interface made of grey bars and circles is the worst outcome; if you cannot build a believable fragment, change direction. Mark each fragment's root element with the attribute data-ui: inside it the product's own conventions apply (1px control borders, small radii, a shadow on its open menu) and the inspector leaves them alone; outside it the house rules hold as usual. data-ui is for cropped fragments only, never for a page wrapper. Do not put the fragment in a browser or laptop frame.

hero.name: Fragment on a shaped stage
hero.blueprint: A neutral ground. The headline occupies the upper-left third: two lines at clamp(52px, 5.2vw, 80px), medium weight, flush left on columns 1–6 at a 40px margin, starting 150px down. One supporting sentence at 18px, max 40ch, follows, then the single action as a small rectangular button. The rest of the screen belongs to one flat stage in a saturated colour: it spans columns 5–12, begins 42% down, and bleeds off the right and bottom edges. Its top-left corner is cut with the product's own shape using `clip-path` (a notch, a chamfer or a tab two columns wide), the only decoration on the page. On the stage, 56px in from its left and top edges, sits the main fragment of the interface at true size with labels at 13–15px, built in HTML and working: one panel or control about 620px wide, cropped by the bottom edge, never a whole window and never inside a browser or laptop frame. Mark its root with data-ui. Navigation is a plain row at 28px from the top: wordmark left and four text links right at 15px. Nothing overlaps the headline.
hero.mobile: The headline sits under the wordmark at 10vw on two lines, followed by the sentence at 16px and the button. The stage comes next at full width, bleeding off both sides and the bottom, its corner cut kept at 72px wide. The fragment sits 16px inside it at true size; if it is wider than the screen the right edge crops it rather than scaling it down.
hero.headline: A plain statement of what the product does in three to six words, two lines of up to about 16 characters each at 5.2vw.

motion.name: Shutter image
motion.description: The one hero or showcase image opens from an edge with a clip-path over about 1.1 seconds while the picture inside settles from 1.12 scale to rest. Use it once, on the image that matters most; later images simply are there. Recipe: 'Image shutter' in references/motion.md.

sections.name: One control, blown up
sections.blueprint: A flat saturated field, full-bleed and 92svh tall, holds one working control from the product: the toggle, slider, segmented switch or record button the whole product turns on. Build it at true proportions with every dimension in em, mark its root data-ui, then raise that root's font-size until the control stands about 46vh tall. Anchor it right of centre so the section's right and bottom edges crop about a fifth of it (overflow: hidden on the section). It keeps its real label and value, now at poster size, and it works: operating it swaps the field between two palette colours and changes one word of the heading. The heading, two to four words at clamp(28px, 2.6vw, 40px), sits top-left on the page margin with one sentence at 17px beneath it. The lower-left third of the field stays empty.
sections.mobile: The field is 86svh. Heading and sentence sit top-left at 26px and 16px. The control is enlarged to about 130vw wide and anchored bottom-left, so the right edge crops its far end while its thumb or active segment stays within reach. It still works and still swaps the field colour.

sections.name: Call and response column
sections.blueprint: The sequence is shown as what you give and what comes back, in one narrow column 560px wide starting at column 4, or on the page's text axis. Three exchanges, 88px apart. Each opens with a sentence at 20px medium that begins with its order word ('First, install it.' 'Then ask for a chart.'). 16px under it, the call: the literal thing the user enters, in a filled panel one tone off the ground, radius 8px, padding 20px. For a developer tool that is real code in `<pre><code>` at 14px with a working copy button; otherwise it is the product's own input holding real typed text. Under the call, indented 56px, the response: a true-size fragment marked data-ui showing what the product returns. The third response is the finished result and breaks out of the column, 760px wide, running to column 12. The heading, two to four words at 28px, sits 56px above the first sentence.
sections.mobile: The column fills the width with 20px margins. Calls and responses stack without the indent; a 24px gap and a lighter panel tone set the response apart. Code panels scroll sideways inside themselves. The final result runs edge to edge at true size, cropped on the right if wider.

sections.name: Staggered fragment cells
sections.blueprint: A three-column grid of six filled cells with 8px gaps, each cell 420–460px tall and filled one tone off the ground, no outlines. Every cell has two parts: a text part (a title at 17px medium and three lines at 15px in the soft ink, 24px padding) and a real fragment of the interface at true size (a control, a menu, a table slice, a swatch strip) docked flush against the opposite edge of the cell and cropped by it. The stagger is the idea: across the first row cells run text-top, fragment-top, text-top; the second row runs the reverse, so fragments form a checkerboard. Fragments differ in shape and size on purpose. The heading, two to four words at 32–40px, sits left-aligned above the grid with 56px beneath it and no supporting line.
sections.mobile: One column of cells at their natural height with 6px gaps. Every cell runs text first, fragment second, but fragments alternate between docking to the left edge and the right edge, and they are allowed to run off the side of the cell at true size instead of shrinking.

sections.name: Figure set by a slider
sections.blueprint: The number is the visitor's own. A flat field at least 88svh tall. Top-left, on the page margin: a question of two to five words at 36–44px that serves as the heading ('How many invoices a month?'). 28px under it, one control from the product at true size, 400px wide, root marked data-ui: a slider with its real label and current value, or a stepper, or a short numeric field, preset to a typical answer. Then a long gap. Bottom-left, on the same edge, the result at clamp(140px, 19vw, 320px), heavy, leading 0.8, tabular numerals, with its unit at 0.22em on the same baseline. It recalculates on every input event from a stated, honest formula. Bottom-right, on the figure's baseline, one sentence at 17px, 30ch wide, says how the figure is worked out. No other figure appears in the section.
sections.mobile: Question at 26px, then the control at full width with a 44px thumb. The figure sits at the bottom at 30vw with its unit beneath it at 20px, both flush left. The working-out sentence follows at 15px. The section is at least 84svh so the gap between control and figure survives.

sections.name: The price, very large
sections.blueprint: One plan, no card. Columns 1–4 hold a heading of two to four words at 28–36px and one paragraph at 17px, top-aligned. Columns 6–12 hold the price as a display figure: numerals at clamp(120px, 16vw, 240px), tight tracking, leading 0.85, with the currency sign at half that size raised to the cap line and the period (per month, once) at 18px beside the last numeral on the baseline. One thing from the page overlaps the numerals by 10–15% of their height: the product photograph, the interface fragment or the motif shape, placed over the top-right of the figure. Beneath the figure, on its left edge, four plain lines at 18px state what is included, one per line, without ticks or bullets, then a single rectangular button. The section is at least 80svh tall with the figure vertically centred.
sections.mobile: The heading and paragraph come first, full width. The figure follows at 34vw, flush left, with the overlapping object tucked at its top-right corner at a third of the screen wide. Included lines at 17px and a full-width button close the block.

sections.name: Accordion of filled tiles
sections.blueprint: A two-part row. Columns 1–4 hold the heading, two to four words at about 4vw, `position: sticky; top: 96px` so it stays while the list scrolls past. Columns 5–12 hold the accordion: each question is a filled tile one step from the page ground, with 8px between tiles, no border and the page's one radius (or its motif's corner). A closed tile is 72px tall with the question at 20px medium on the left, 24px padding, and on the right a plus sign drawn from two 3px bars 16px long. The open tile switches to the accent colour with its assigned ink, the plus becomes a minus by rotating one bar, and the answer appears at 17px, no wider than 52ch. Build each tile as `<details>` with a shared `name` so one opens at a time. Six to nine tiles.
sections.mobile: The heading sits above at 9vw, not sticky. Tiles run full width with 6px gaps, questions at 18px wrapping to two lines, closed height at least 64px. The open tile keeps the accent colour, and answers are set at 16px with 20px padding.

sections.name: The action tile
sections.blueprint: The close is one row of the board. Three filled tiles sit side by side with 8–14px gaps, all 360px tall and sharing one radius: a wide centre tile spanning columns 3–10 in the accent colour, flanked by two narrow tiles (columns 1–2 and 11–12) that run off the left and right viewport edges, as if the row had been cropped from a longer one. The centre tile holds, left-aligned and vertically centred with 40px padding: a heading of three to five words at 40px, two lines at 17px, and the action. The action is either one rectangular button or an email field 420px wide in the paper colour with the submit button nested inside its right end. The flanking tiles hold no text: one is a photograph covering the tile, the other a flat palette colour. No shadows, no outlines.
sections.mobile: The accent tile runs full width, about 300px tall, heading at 28px, field and button stacked at full width. The two flanking tiles follow beneath as a pair, each half width and 120px tall, with the same gap and the same radius.

sections.name: A single quiet line
sections.blueprint: No footer block at all. After at least 30svh of empty page ground, one baseline 30px above the bottom edge carries three items in the page's ordinary small text size (14–16px), the same size and weight as the navigation: at the left margin, what this is in three or four words; centred, two to five links separated by 24px of space; at the right margin, the year and a privacy link. Use a three-column grid (1fr auto 1fr) so the centre group is truly centred whatever the side lengths. No logo, no background change, no line above it, no columns. Links are in the full ink; the rest in the softer ink. If the page has a narrow text column, the three items may instead sit on that column's left edge as one wrapped line. The restraint only works if the page above has already made its invitation.
sections.mobile: Three short lines at 14px on the left margin with 8px between them: the description, the links on one wrapped line, then year and privacy. Links stay in the full ink. Leave 20svh of empty ground above and 24px below.

references.name: Uni
references.idea: The product lives in the laptop notch, so the page's navigation is a black notch and the hero is a laptop outline whose notch opens into the app.
references.hero: White page with the hero as a rounded-corner panel inset 24px on all sides, filled with a grainy pastel gradient (pink-peach centre, sky blue down the right edge, orange lower-left). A black pill 300×44px sits top-centre like a laptop notch, holding only the app icon; it is the entire nav. Centred below: a hand-scrawled caps eyebrow, a two-line 48px (3.3vw) headline, two white pill download buttons side by side, one line of tiny grey reassurance. The bottom 40% is a thick black outline of a laptop screen, 960px wide, cropped by the fold, its notch expanded into a dark input bar playing the demo.
references.type: Instrument Sans 500 at 48px with -0.025em tracking for headings; Geist 16px for UI and 12–13px captions. Eyebrows are hand-scrawled marker capitals, irregular and tilted. Only three sizes on the page; the headline is just three times the body.
references.colour: #ffffff #fbdad6 #fce6db #aacbec #f9a070 #000000 — Colour lives only in the hero's grainy pastel gradient; below it the page is white and #fbfbfb with black text. Buttons are near-white pills; the notch is the single black mass.
references.imagery: No photos. A laptop reduced to a thick black rounded outline frames a looping screen recording of the notch UI; eight line icons below. The gradient has visible film grain.
references.layout: Everything on the centre axis. The laptop frame's side strokes continue down the page as hairline rules, so the mockup becomes a 960px content column holding tabs, an icon grid and an FAQ. Three short sections, generous white space, minimal footer.

sections.description: Directly under the device a segmented pill control with three tabs switches the demo. Then a hand-scrawled two-word eyebrow, a centred 32px heading, and a four-by-two grid of thin line icons, each with a two-line 12px centred caption. No cards, borders or backgrounds — just icons on white with about 100px between columns, all inside the hairline-bounded column.

A #fbfbfb band inside the same column. The heading straddles the band's top edge. One rounded, hairline-bordered container holds nine rows separated by hairlines; each row has a 12px medium question at left and a thin plus sign at right. Beneath, a two-line micro footer centred: Roman-numeral year, tiny wordmark, a three-word credit, two legal links.

steal: Shape the navigation like the product's own hardware habitat (here a black notch pill) so the nav itself demonstrates the product.
Extend a device mockup's side strokes down the page as hairline rules so the mockup becomes the content column.
Use a hand-scrawled marker eyebrow above a clean grotesk headline to add one human note to a system-clean page.

references.name: Rows
references.idea: Radical understatement: a product about simple lists is sold with a 27px headline, 12px copy and a column of small live demos, each proving one interaction.
references.hero: Warm off-white page, almost empty. Everything hangs on one vertical line 27% in from the left. A small striped-letter logo mark sits there near the top; 220px lower comes a two-line headline at only 27px (under 2vw), then three lines of 13px body about 370px wide, then a near-black rectangular button with 4px corners beside a text link with an arrow. A single grey sign-in link sits in the top-right corner; there is no navigation bar. More than 80% of the viewport is blank. At the bottom edge the first feature module peeks in: grey demo panel left, short text column right.
references.type: Suisse Intl only, weight 450–500, tracking −0.04em. Headline 27px, feature headings about 16px on two lines, body 12px. Three sizes in total, no uppercase and no display moment; hierarchy comes from weight and empty space alone.
references.colour: #f5f6f1 #e6e7e1 #1a191d #ffffff #c7372f #3aa56a — Warm paper off-white with slightly darker grey-green demo panels and near-black type; colour appears only inside the UI as priority dots, outlined status pills and one green or red action button.
references.imagery: No pictures: small live-rendered fragments of the app (two or three white list rows with dots, status pills, avatars and a visible cursor) sit in flat grey panels of fixed 368px width with barely rounded corners.
references.layout: One content block about 650px wide, offset left of centre, repeated down the page: 368px demo panel plus a 245px text column, top-aligned, separated by 200px or more of empty space. The logo mark sticks to the top-left corner on scroll. Footer is one line.

sections.description: The repeating module: a flat grey panel roughly 368px wide and 120–190px tall holding a tiny mock list (white rows with 6px radius, a coloured numbered dot at left, task title, an outlined status pill, an avatar, a chevron) and often a cursor mid-action. To its right, 20px away and top-aligned, a medium-weight heading of one or two lines and two short paragraphs at 11–12px in a column only 245px wide. Modules never alternate sides; they stack with large gaps.

The closing block keeps the same narrow measure: a three-line paragraph at 13px, then the identical button and arrow-link pair from the hero, left-aligned on the text column's axis. After a long gap a single hairline spans the 650px block and under it sits one row of tiny footer text: brand line at left, six links and a copyright strung along the right.

steal: Set the headline at near-body size (under 2vw) and let empty space, not scale, give it importance.
Explain each feature with a tiny cropped fragment of real UI in a fixed-width flat panel, one interaction per panel, with the cursor left visible.
Hang the whole page on one off-centre left edge and never break it, logo and footer included.

references.name: Fynza
references.idea: Bookings are drawn as avatar dots whose orange flow lines merge into a single vertical spine, which then runs down the page as the axis for the partner list, the cash-flow timeline and the step cards.
references.hero: Warm grey ground with a fine white dot texture and a peach gradient bleeding down from the top edge. A floating white pill navbar 80% wide holds the logo left and a language switch plus outlined and orange pill buttons right. Centred stack: a white pill badge with overlapping partner-logo dots, a two-line extra-bold uppercase headline at 4.2vw in slate navy with two words in orange, two lines of grey 18px text, an orange pill button. Around the button five round avatar photos with small booking labels sit at staggered heights across the full width; thin orange curves, two dashed, flow down from each and converge at bottom centre.
references.type: Golos Text only: weight 800 uppercase at 60px for every section headline with slight negative tracking, 18px regular grey body, about 24px semibold for card titles, tiny uppercase captions. A wide extended logo wordmark. Roughly four sizes; hierarchy relies on weight and colour.
references.colour: #edecea #ffffff #f4bba8 #f2561d #3f4f6e #1a2e7a — Warm grey and white with peach gradients fading in at section tops and bottoms; orange carries buttons, flow lines and highlighted headline words; one deep royal-navy slab near the end.
references.imagery: Round avatar photos, partner logo discs, sunny travel photographs inside rounded cards with white UI snippets floating on top, and illustrated vintage postage stamps tilted and scattered around the final call to action.
references.layout: Centred container of about 1150px; every section opens with a small white pill label and a two-line uppercase headline. A single orange vertical line runs through the page centre linking hero, logo list, timeline and step cards. Sections alternate grey, peach fade and one navy slab.

sections.description: Directly under the hero the converged orange line becomes a vertical spine and partner brands hang off it in two columns: logo then name on the left, name then logo on the right. Rows are separated by dashed horizontal rules with small orange dots where they cross the spine. There is no heading, so it reads as a continuation of the hero diagram.

Problem timeline on the centre spine: small rounded-square chips labelled by week sit on the line. Events alternate left and right, each joined to its chip by a dashed horizontal line ending in a small coloured amount tag (red for outflow, green for income), with a bold label and two lines of grey text. A red-tinted rounded note sits on the spine as the conclusion while the background fades to saturated peach.

Three large white rounded cards stacked on the spine, each a two-column split that alternates sides: on one side an orange numbered disc, a three-line semibold title and a small grey paragraph; on the other a rounded travel photograph with a white UI card or a cluster of logo discs floating over it. The orange line passes behind the gaps between cards.

Dotted peach-to-white field with a centred two-line uppercase headline, one word in orange, and an orange pill button. Six illustrated vintage travel stamps and round stickers are scattered around it at slight rotations, three above and three below, some tucked under the navbar. A tiny two-line legal footer sits directly underneath, centred, with no separate footer band.

steal: Turn the hero illustration's lines into a page-long spine: let the curves converge at the fold and continue as the axis for the next section's list and timeline.
Show the customer's own unit of value (a booking with name, party size and price) as small avatar chips instead of a dashboard screenshot.
End on a themed sticker scatter (illustrated stamps at varied tilt) around the last call to action rather than a plain coloured band.
